The supplied search results report this price and a coupon test dated November 2, 2026. I haven't independently verified the checkout price. <Cite ref="turn980558view0"/>

## How it compares

| Model | Listed price | Capacity | AC output |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | $854.05 with code | 2,048Wh | 2,400W |
| Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO | $676.16 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W |
| OUPES Mega 2 Pro | $699 | 2,048Wh | 2,500W |
| Renogy PowerStation 2000 | $799 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | $999 direct | 2,042Wh | 2,200W |

Prices are from the supplied search results, primarily checked in October–November 2026. <Cite ref="turn980558view0"/>

## What matters for your RV

The BLUETTI AC200L has a built-in TT-30 outlet, but its 2,400W inverter supplies approximately **20A at 120V, not the full 30A** of conventional RV shore power.

It should handle lights, a water pump, an RV refrigerator, and occasional coffee-maker use, provided the combined load stays within its output limit. It isn't a reliable choice for running a typical rooftop air conditioner for extended periods.

The 1,200W solar input is useful for off-grid trips, though actual charging depends on sunlight and panels.

**Bottom line:** Choose the BLUETTI AC200L for its RV-friendly features. If lowest price matters more, the **Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at $676.16** is a compelling alternative with the same listed battery capacity and AC output. <Cite ref="turn980558view0"/>
